name: PLEC-related Intermediate Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex without Extracutaneous Involvement
aliases: Intermediate Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex due to Plectin Mutation
PLEC-associated EBS Intermediate Type without Systemic Manifestations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex

criteria.description: Recurrent skin blistering and erosions predominantly on hands and feet triggered by minor trauma
Immunofluorescence mapping showing intraepidermal cleavage within basal keratinocytes
Identification of pathogenic biallelic mutations in the PLEC gene
Lack of extracutaneous involvement such as muscular or mucosal abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent blistering clinically plus either immunofluorescence confirmation of intraepidermal cleavage or identification of pathogenic PLEC mutations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Muscle and mucosal involvement must be excluded to confirm absence of extracutaneous manifestations.

laboratory: Immunofluorescence mapping demonstrating intraepidermal cleavage within basal keratinocytes
Histopathology showing basal keratinocyte cytolysis and blister formation
other: Negative muscle biopsy and absence of muscular dystrophy signs to exclude extracutaneous involvement

distinguishingFeatures: Mutations in KRT5 gene instead of PLEC
Blistering predominantly basal but may have different severity and distribution
No plectin protein abnormalities on immunostaining
Presence of muscular dystrophy and extracutaneous involvement
More severe phenotype with muscle weakness
Systemic manifestations absent in PLEC-related intermediate EBS without extracutaneous involvement

redFlags: Onset of muscle weakness or hypotonia indicating extracutaneous involvement
Rapidly progressive blistering with systemic symptoms
references: Fine JD, et al. Inherited epidermolysis bullosa: updated recommendations on diagnosis and classification. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2020.
Has C, et al. Plectin-related epidermolysis bullosa simplex: clinical and molecular findings. Br J Dermatol. 2012.
Orphanet: PLEC-related intermediate epidermolysis bullosa simplex without extracutaneous involvement. ORPHA:79401.
